General Strike Brings Belarusian Economic Activity to a Standstill

MINSK — A sweeping general strike has gripped Belarus since early Wednesday morning, as workers in transport, manufacturing, education, and healthcare sectors walked off the job in coordinated protest over wage policies and working conditions. The strike, organized by the United Labour Front and supported by several sectoral unions, has disrupted daily life and economic activity across the country.

Public transport services in Minsk and other major cities are running at minimal capacity. “We are operating only 25% of our normal bus and tram routes,” said Yelena Kalinina, spokesperson for the Minsk City Transit Authority. “Many drivers and conductors have joined the strike, and we urge passengers to use alternative means if possible.”

Major factories in the industrial hub of Gomel, including the state-run BelMach Engineering and the private Agrotechno Group, have suspended production. Reports from local union leaders estimate that up to 70% of assembly line workers are participating in the strike.

At the same time, schools and universities have canceled classes, with the Ministry of Education confirming that most teaching staff have not reported for duty. “We are in ongoing talks with union representatives to resolve the situation,” said Deputy Minister Pavel Zubarev. Hospital services remain limited to emergency care only, as nurses and non-emergency staff join the strike.

Small businesses are also affected, with many shops and cafes closing their doors in solidarity. The Belarusian Chamber of Commerce has called the strike “unprecedented in scale,” warning that extended disruption could cost the national economy tens of millions of rubles per day.

Natalia Savitskaya, a spokesperson for the United Labour Front, stated, “Our members are demanding fair wages and safer conditions. We are prepared to continue the strike until our voices are heard.”

Government officials are urging calm and promising dialogue, but as of Thursday afternoon, no agreement has been reached. Analysts say the widespread participation and cross-sectoral impact of the strike mark a significant moment in Belarus’s labor history, with no clear end yet in sight.
